title: Level 3 (Advanced) - D-15
notes:
West leads the ♠Q against 3NT. South has 5 sure winners outside of clubs (the ♠A, ♠K, ♥A, ♦A, and ♦K). South should look for the safest possible way to ensure 4 club winners.

It would be a mistake to duck the first round of spades as a heart shift from West would not be welcome. South should win the ♠K at trick 1 and lay down the ♣A (to guard against a singleton ♣K with West). When both defenders follow small, South should cross to the dummy in diamonds and lead a second round of clubs toward the closed hand. When East follows small, South plays the ♣Q or ♣J.

If clubs are 3-2, South will have no further problems. If West discards on the second round of clubs, South can cross back to the dummy and lead another club toward the South hand. The recommended line of play allows South to make the contract any time it is possible to do so.
